entry.title: Building tomorrow’s workforce in the heart of D.C.

media:group.media:title: Building tomorrow’s workforce in the heart of D.C.
media:group.media:description:
Virginia Tech’s growing innovation network in the greater Washington, D.C., area prepares students for the workforce of tomorrow and brings together leading researchers, industry partners, and national policymakers to address some of the world’s most urgent challenges. In this vibrant hub, faculty and students work with industry to advance research and innovation in artificial intelligence, wireless technology, quantum computing, national security and other emerging fields. Through project-based learning and partnerships, students gain experience solving real-world problems while faculty research drives meaningful impact.
Guided by our land-grant mission, Ut Prosim (That I May Serve), Virginia Tech brings together talent, ideas, and partnerships to create lasting impact.

entry.title: Assistant Secretary of Energy visits Virginia Tech to see the future of mining

media:group.media:title: Assistant Secretary of Energy visits Virginia Tech to see the future of mining
media:group.media:description: During a visit to Virginia Tech, Assistant Secretary of Energy for the U.S. Department of Energy Audrey Robertson, highlighted the growing need for mining engineers. The visit showcased how Virginia Tech is preparing the next generation of engineers through interdisciplinary education that combines mining, robotics, artificial intelligence, autonomy, and wireless communications.

entry.title: Virginia Peanuts: Growing the Best from the Ground Up

media:group.media:title: Virginia Peanuts: Growing the Best from the Ground Up
media:group.media:description:
Virginia peanuts are famous for being large, gourmet-style peanuts that are often sold and roasted in the shell. They play a vital role in the region’s agricultural economy, generating millions of dollars annually and supporting local businesses, jobs, and farming communities.
Researchers at Virginia Tech's Tidewater Agricultural Research and Extension Center, Extension specialists, and producers work together to improve peanut production through field trials, variety evaluations, disease-resistance testing, harvest-timing recommendations, and quality assessments. Their research helps growers adopt the best management practices, increase yields, and produce high-quality peanuts, while continuing Virginia’s long-standing legacy as a leader in peanut production and innovation.

entry.title: Can we save an imperiled pollinator?

media:group.media:title: Can we save an imperiled pollinator?
media:group.media:description:
Monarch butterflies make an extraordinary annual migration across eastern North America, but their populations have declined significantly in recent decades. Researchers in the College of Natural Resources and Environment Conservation Management Institute are working to better understand their migration routes by using radio transmitters, providing information that could help guide conservation efforts, reduce pesticide exposure and identify areas where additional habitat could make a difference.
Research in the School of Plant and Environmental Sciences is exploring ways to dissuade monarchs from laying eggs on milkweed that’s been sprayed by pesticides. By testing compounds that alter how milkweed reflects ultraviolet light, researchers hope to help monarchs recognize and avoid contaminated plants. Protecting monarchs is also something anyone can take part in, whether by creating a small garden, planting monarch-friendly vegetation or simply adding a few potted plants at home.

entry.title: Virginia Tech students unearth the story of Earth’s history

media:group.media:title: Virginia Tech students unearth the story of Earth’s history
media:group.media:description: Virginia Tech department of geosciences researchers and students traveled to Arizona to uncover fossils preserved for more than 215 million years. These Triassic fossils reveal how ecosystems responded to climate change, helping scientists better understand the past, the present, and what may lie ahead. Along the way, students gain hands-on experience in discovery, data collection, and scientific exploration.

entry.title: Teachers become fossil hunters alongside Virginia Tech researchers

media:group.media:title: Teachers become fossil hunters alongside Virginia Tech researchers
media:group.media:description: The DIG Field School pairs leading researchers in paleontology and geology with educators from across the country to spend four days learning how paleontologists uncover fossils, collect scientific data, and reconstruct Earth's history. Virginia Tech department of geosciences faculty and students work with participants to experience the scientific process firsthand and bring those lessons back to inspire the next generation of scientists.

media:group.media:title: From hens to Hokies
media:group.media:description:
Students at Virginia Tech are gaining hands-on experience in poultry production through an egg enterprise. Students help care for the chickens, collect eggs, and learn how to process, grade, clean, and check eggs for quality. Along the way, they develop practical skills in animal care, flock management, and food production that can help prepare them for careers in animal science and related fields.
The eggs produced through the program also make their way back into the Virginia Tech community. Dining Services incorporates the eggs into campus food service, while The Market of Virginia Tech, the university’s food pantry, provides eggs to students experiencing food insecurity. By connecting experiential learning with campus dining and food access, the egg enterprise gives students a firsthand look at the journey from farm to table while creating an opportunity for students to help fellow Hokies.

media:group.media:title: Celebrating women in agriculture
media:group.media:description: The United Nations declared 2026 the International Year of the Woman Farmer (IYWF 2026). The Year spotlights the essential roles women play across agrifood systems, from production to trade. Women farmers are central to food security, nutrition and economic resilience. The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences Global and the Global Agricultural Productivity (GAP) Initiative celebrate the IYWF 2026 with the goal of raising awareness and promoting actions to improve women’s livelihoods worldwide.
